title: Smoky Beef and Vegetable Sliders
changes_from_base: Instead of patties, a small amount of browned beef mince is stretched with onion, red pepper, carrot and courgette and simmered in a smoky paprika tomato sauce, like a tidy sloppy Joe, then spooned into slider buns; cider vinegar sharpens it at the end.
summary: A thick, tomato-based filling laden with vegetables and fragrant with smoked paprika and hints of vinegary heat, served in small soft rolls.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
small red pepper, deseeded and diced
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Heat 30 ml extra-virgin olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high, add 225 g lean beef mince with ½ tsp salt and ½ tsp ground black pepper and cook, breaking it up, for about 5 min until browned; remove with a slotted spoon onto a plate.

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Cook 1 diced medium onion, 1 diced small red pepper and 1 diced small peeled carrot in the same pan for 5-10 min until soft.

steps.title: Spice
steps.text: Stir in 1 diced medium courgette and 2 finely chopped garlic cloves, then add 1½ tsp salt and 1½ tsp hot smoked paprika.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Pour in a 400 g tin of chopped tomatoes and 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, return the browned beef and simmer for about 10 min until thick and the beef is cooked through to 71 °C.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Taste and adjust the seasoning with ½ tsp salt and 1½ tsp cider vinegar, adding more vinegar to taste if desired.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the filling generously onto slider bun bottoms and top with bun tops.

tips: Break the beef into fine pieces whilst browning so it distributes evenly through the final filling
Worcestershire sauce contains anchovies (fish); check the label
Taste before adjusting the vinegar, as it can quickly overpower the other flavours
storage: Leftovers keep chilled for 2 days; reheat until piping hot before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
